text:
Anya Petrov: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking through a KMS escrow pattern for on-prem/offline package signing. We need a minimal operator UX for rotating signing keys without sending private key material offsite. Thoughts? :key:
Matt Cheng: Are you proposing ephemeral escrow blobs per-release?
Anya Petrov: Yeah — operator generates per-release wrapping key (HSM or YubiKey), we store the wrapped key blob in the customer vault but escrow under split-KMS so Redwood can assist recovery without holding plaintext.
Julie Park: Concern: escrowed blob is single point of compromise. Recommend threshold encryption (Shamir) or multisig release so recovery needs both customer and Redwood ops approvals.
Samir Patel: Agreed. For air-gapped sites we should support an "operator handoff" flow: create QR-signed-manifest -> operator scans on an offline machine with a hardware token -> exports an encrypted blob to USB. Keep blobs short-lived and versioned. :warning:
Julie Park: UX idea: tool emits `escrow.json` with minimal fields: `wrapped_key_b64`, `expiry`, `nonce`, `signer_pub`. Example snippet:
```
{
  "wrapped_key_b64": "...",
  "expiry": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z",
  "nonce": "abc123",
  "signer_pub": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----..."
}
```
Samir Patel: And server-side we validate provider signatures + require TPM attestation from the operator host before accepting an escrowed blob. That cuts down on rogue USB insertion attacks.
Anya Petrov: ops-bot: can you run a quick schema check on that payload?
ops-bot: escrow schema v1 validated against `escrow-schema.json` — no errors.
Matt Cheng: Also add a policy layer: escrow release should be gated (A/B approval, audit record, time-lock). Automate rotation to rewrap blobs on major model or runtime upgrades.
Anya Petrov: Great feedback. I'll sketch the flow (handoff, escrow-store, recovery) + short threat model and propose a minimal API for `redwood-agent` to consume escrow blobs. Will post RFC draft tomorrow. Thanks! :+1:
